evals.prompt: Our Rust API's Docker release build takes about 35 minutes on an x86_64 machine because Buildx targets linux/arm64 and runs cargo build inside the target container. Propose a safe migration to Zig/cargo-zigbuild and a fair way to measure the result. Don't deploy anything.
evals.expected_output: A repository-aware migration outline that moves Rust compilation to the host/CI runner, leaves Buildx for image packaging, specifies target/runtime ABI checks, and compares equivalent cache and resource conditions without deploying.
expectations: Separates host-side cargo-zigbuild compilation from Buildx image packaging.
Calls out target triple, libc baseline, and native dependency/sysroot requirements.
Requires comparable cache states and reports compile time separately from total image time.
Does not deploy or recommend compiling on a production server.

evals.prompt: A Rust service uses openssl-sys and must keep its current OpenSSL TLS behavior, but an amd64 CI runner needs to produce a Debian ARM64 image. Is adding the Rust target enough? Give the cross-build setup and checks you'd require before shipping.
evals.expected_output: An explanation that a Rust target alone does not provide target OpenSSL headers/libraries; describe a target-matched sysroot and pkg-config environment, preserve TLS behavior, and verify ELF architecture, ABI, shared libraries, and runtime smoke behavior.
expectations: Explains why host OpenSSL development files cannot be used for an ARM64 link.
Specifies target-aware sysroot and pkg-config configuration.
Does not silently switch TLS implementations or claim the target triple alone solves native dependencies.
Includes binary and runtime compatibility validation.

evals.prompt: A cold ARM64 Docker build took about 42 minutes, while a cached cargo zigbuild run took 0.7 seconds. My workstation is already under heavy load. Can I tell the team we got a 1000x speedup and run a full no-cache Buildx build now to confirm?
evals.expected_output: Rejects the unqualified speedup claim because cold and cached measurements are incomparable; avoids launching another resource-heavy build on an already-loaded workstation and proposes a staged, one-at-a-time comparison with isolated caches and bounded resource use.
expectations: States that cached and cold timings cannot support the requested speedup claim.
Does not initiate or urge an immediate heavy build while the workstation is loaded.
Proposes a controlled comparison and distinguishes Rust compilation from end-to-end packaging.
Records cache state, target, versions, flags, and resource limits.
